subject: Linguistics
title: Mayan Glyphs
description: A micro-lesson that makes Mayan Glyphs usable.

hook.text: Mayan glyphs were once thought to be purely symbolic—until researchers proved they encoded full language.

buildup.text: The Maya developed the most complete writing system in pre-Columbian America.

discovery.text: Yuri Knorozov showed in 1952 that glyphs mixed logograms and syllabic signs—like Egyptian hieroglyphs.

twist.text: Spanish colonizers burned almost all Mayan books—only four codices survived the destruction.

climax.text: Today, about 80% of Mayan glyphs have been deciphered, revealing history, astronomy, and poetry.

punchline.text: A civilization's voice, almost silenced, speaks again.

quiz.question: What did Knorozov discover about Mayan glyphs?
options: They mixed logograms and syllabic signs
